title: Division Algorithm
description: Expresses the relationship between dividend, divisor, quotient and remainder.

example.question: Find the remainder when 29 is divided by 6.

note: The remainder is always less than the divisor.

title: Range of Remainder
description: The remainder is always non-negative and strictly less than the divisor.

example.question: Can the remainder be 8 when dividing by 8?
example.solution: No. The largest possible remainder is 7.

note: A remainder can never be equal to or greater than the divisor.

title: Divisible Number
description: If the remainder is zero, the dividend is exactly divisible by the divisor.

example.question: Find the remainder when 48 is divided by 6.

note: A remainder of zero means exact division.

title: Remainder of Sum
formula: (a+b) mod n = [(a mod n)+(b mod n)] mod n
description: The remainder of a sum can be obtained from the remainders of the individual numbers.

example.question: Find the remainder when 27 + 35 is divided by 5.

title: Remainder of Product
formula: (ab) mod n = [(a mod n)(b mod n)] mod n
description: The remainder of a product depends on the remainders of its factors.

example.question: Find the remainder when 13 × 17 is divided by 5.
